newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen weak at open, eye on U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen weak at open, eye on U.S. CPI.

--------------------MARKET COMMENT---------------------------- * Toronto stocks were expected to open lower despite Canada's lower-than-expected CPI growth as the Canadian dollar slipped overnight. * Market will take its direction from U.S. CPI.
Toronto stocks were expected to trade lower at the open on Tuesday despite lower than expected Canadian consumer prices data as the Canadian dollar weakened overnight.
But analysts said North American markets would take their direction from U.S. consumer price data due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

"Our numbers are fine, but we've got a lot of numbers coming out of the U.S. today," said Katherine Beattie, technical analyst at MMS International. She said markets will need a low number to avoid a second day of losses.
A Reuters survey of economists predicts a 0.2 percent rise in May from April. Core CPI was expected to rise 0.2 percent after a 0.3 percent gain in April.
"I think the risk is we'll have (another weak day)...golds are certainly not helping us," Beattie said.
But she said any weakness should be short-lived as markets remain in an uptrend.
Toronto stocks slipped 13.13 points on Monday to close at 6537.47 points as 11 out of the 14 sub-sectors of the Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 index fell.
Earlier this morning Statistics Canada said Canada's unadjusted May consumer price index rose 0.1 percent in the month and 1.5. percent in the year. Core CPI rose 1.7 percent year-on-year.

Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast, on average, the unadjusted CPI to rise 0.2 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 1.6 percent year-over-year rise in the all-items and a 1.8. percent increase in the core CPI.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---
* Bombardier Corp said early on Tuesday it won a US$1.4 billion contract from AMR Corp's American Eagle regional airline affiliate for 25 Canadian Regional Jets, with options on another 25.

* Stampeder Exploration Ltd on Monday announced a stock offering and a big increase in spending. Stampeder said it planned to use the proceeds of its offering to fund stepped up heavy oil drilling and not takeovers.
